shortName: Geisel School of Medicine at Dartmouth

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The Geisel School of Medicine graduates the complete physician—one who excels in the basic sciences, delivers outstanding clinical care, discovers and shares new knowledge, and works to improve systems of health care delivery. We believe a diverse and inclusive community enhances our mission of providing an exceptional education to tackle the evolving challenges in health care.  Our ability to understand health and disease and provide optimal care for all patients we serve requires that we recruit, support, and retain students, trainees, faculty, and staff that encompass the full diversity of our population.  The Office of Diversity, Inclusion & Community Engagement provides active advising and support to our diverse community. For additional information please go to the following link: https://geiselmed.dartmouth.edu/dice/.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A leave of absence, permitting the student to leave the curriculum for periods up to one year, may be granted.  .  A maximum of two leaves of absence (each up to 12 months in length) will be granted to a student.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Extracurricular activities are integral to the Geisel experience. Through a wide range of community service-learning opportunities, Geisel students play an important role in addressing unmet health needs in the community. Student interest groups are organized around Community Health, Health Policy, Human Rights, Sustainability, Climate Change, Disability advocacy, and Medical Education, along with over 25 other interest groups. Athletics and wellness activities are prominent including intramurals, sporting competitions, performing arts groups, and cooking clubs. Students are supported to form new groups to meet their individualized interests. A full list can be found here: https://geiselmed.dartmouth.edu/student-gov/student-groups/.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Geisel School of Medicine at Dartmouth is located in Hanover, NH. Dartmouth has a long tradition of academic excellence, a reputation for especially close faculty/student interactions, and a strong sense of community. The College and surrounding communities are home to a wealth of cultural and recreational attractions, including the Hopkins Center for the Arts, The Hood Museum, the Dartmouth Film Society, the Dartmouth Outing Club, Northern Stage, and JAG Productions. There is easy access to the pristine New England landscape and a wide range of outdoor activities including hiking, skiing, walking, kayaking and more (see https://outdoors.dartmouth.edu/dartmouth-outing-club/about-doc or https://dartmouthskiway.com/) . On campus, the gym is available to all students along with access to the woodworking shop, jewelry studio and ceramics studio.
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
Housing is available both on and off campus.  Please see https://realestate.dartmouth.edu for more information and photos.  You can also check Geisel's Facebook page for listings: http://www.facebook.com/pages/Dartmouth-College-Real-Estate-Office/372835284362 . 
Housing is provided for required clerkships in Phase 2 if the clerkship site is more than one hour away from campus.

medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: The Office of Advising and Accessibility supports our learners with disabilities. For more information, please visit their website: https://geiselmed.dartmouth.edu/goaaa/getting-started/about/
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Within Geisel's Office of Student Life, there is a Program Manager for Student Wellness and Engagement who works with Geisel students to develop and implement student mental health and wellbeing programming. The programming is organized around eight wellness domains - emotional, physical, occupational, social, spiritual, intellectual, environmental, and financial. Along with the manager, Geisel Student Government has student mental health and wellness representatives for each class.
 
There is also a full-time Case Manager for Student Well-Being who supports students with any mental health or wellbeing concerns or students in crisis. The Case Manager helps navigate resources within Geisel, at Dartmouth, and throughout the Upper Valley Community.
 
Geisel and Dartmouth College provide the following resources for Mental Health Counseling:
-Dartmouth College Health Service provides free, confidential counseling for students located in NH and VT, as well as 24-hour crisis counselors.
-Geisel Counseling Service provides free, confidential counseling for Geisel students located in NH, VT and CA for in-person and telehealth counseling services.
-Uwill Teletherapy Service provides free, confidential teletherapy services for students anywhere the student is located, as well as Uhelp for crisis support.
 
For more information: https://geiselmed.dartmouth.edu/students/student-wellness-resources/. [geiselmed.dartmouth.edu]
Dartmouth's Commitment to Care, outlines a comprehensive strategic plan for student mental health and wellbeing.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
We encourage our students to lead balanced lives, working collaboratively to create a healthy community that benefits both the students and their future patients.

Our mission is to create a supportive environment in which students can flourish as they transition into medical professionals who are caring, compassionate, and responsible world citizens. We strive to foster in each student a sense of social and professional responsibility that engenders the trust and confidence of the public and complements the exceptional clinical training for which graduates of Geisel are known.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Geisel School of Medicine values strong clinical skills training.  We send students to clinical preceptor sites beginning in Phase 1.  To accomplish this, we have sites up to an hour away. Personal transport and a driver’s license are necessary as free public transport is limited and only to certain locations.
medSchoolStudLife.additionalSupportProgrameName: Learning Collaboratives were established in 2025 with an emphasis on sustained mentorship and character education. Learn more at: https://geiselmed.dartmouth.edu/students/learning-collaboratives/.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Appropriate professional dress is expected in the hospital and clinical settings and for any sessions involving patients and/or community members.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Faculty are easily accessible. Support Services provides tutoring/review sessions; study strategies; counseling/advising, with referrals for more intensive support; USMLE board review strategies.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: “On Doctoring”, our clinical skills course, begins with mentored practice employing standardized patients to develop clinical skills, transitioning to direct patient interaction in spring of Phase 1.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Small group sessions predominate - labs, Team-Based Learning, Case-Based Learning, Problem-Based Learning, and flipped classroom sessions.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: There are 8 required clerkships which last 4-8 weeks. 6 clerkships are usually done in Phase 2 with one elective.  Subinternship(s) are required depending on the specialty field (usually in Phase 3).
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: There is no formal academic prematriculation program, but orientation takes place the week before classes begin.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: Students are not formally ranked in any phase of the curriculum.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Lectures comprise less than 40% of the curriculum.  Attendance is expected with some sessions designated as required. Required sessions involving patient panels are not recorded.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Geisel’s curriculum provides a strong foundation in the basic sciences, exceptional clinical training and experiences, and broad coverage of health care delivery sciences. The curriculum prepares students to become complete physicians through a carefully integrated four-year experience. Our graduates will:
•	Excel in the basic sciences
•	Deliver evidence-based, high-quality clinical care in partnership with patients, families, and communities
•	Discover and share new knowledge
•	Improve the system of healthcare in which they work
Across three curriculum Phases, students are prepared for future careers across the entire spectrum of medical practice including all clinical specialties and subspecialties, research in academic health centers, rural and urban settings, and diverse patient populations. Phase 1 is 16 months focusing on foundational sciences in organs system-based course. Phase 2 is 12 months of required clinical clerkships and electives. Phase 3 is 15 months to explore and prepare for residency.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Opportunities for students to become involved in primary care include the Rural Health, Urban Health, Community Health interest groups,  the local free medical clinic for the underserved, and the Albert Schweitzer Fellowship. Programs are supported by the Departments of Medical Education, Internal Medicine, Pediatrics and Community & Family Medicine, along with the Offices of Student Affairs and of Diversity, Inclusion & Student Engagement.  Dartmouth Health maintains a large network of community-based primary care clinics around the region that serve as sites for medical student engagement.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Geisel School of Medicine provides research opportunities for students in basic, translational, public health, and clinical outcomes research projects. Students join research projects conducted at the Norris Cotton Cancer Center, the Dartmouth Institute for Health Policy and Clinical Practice, the White River Junction VA Medical Center, and Dartmouth-Hitchcock. There is an 8-week summer break between Y1 and Y2 during which students engage in these opportunities. Historically, 80-90% of Geisel students participate in research during medical school. Geisel has an Office of Medical Student Research with a dedicated faculty assistant dean and director to help students learn and navigate the process of conducting research.
More information can be found here: https://geiselmed.dartmouth.edu/student-research/.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Block scheduling during Phase 1; clerkships, electives and capstone during Phase 2 and 3.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Currently, approximately 70% of students participate in a broad range of community-service projects both medically and non-medically related.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: A research requirement is currently built into the Population Health course. Historically, approximately 80-90% of students completed a research experience regardless of the new requirement.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Dartmouth-Hitchcock;  VT VA Hospital; CA Pacific Medical Center; Children’s Hospital Orange County; Fort Defiance Indian Hospital; Navajo Medical Center;  Valdez Medical Center.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:
Phase 1 (Preclinical): Pass/Fail
Phase 2 (Core Clerkships): Honors /Pass /Fail
Phase 3 (Sub-Is/Electives): Honors /High Pass /Pass /Fail

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Founded in 1797, the Geisel School of Medicine at Dartmouth is the fourth oldest medical school in the country. A faculty of  2,384  affords ample opportunity for individual instruction and collaboration. From their first month at Geisel, students gain hands-on clinical experience to care for a broad array of patient populations.  Clinical teaching affiliates include Dartmouth-Hitchcock Medical Center, the White River VA Medical Center, California Pacific Medical Center, Indian Health Services centers, and other sites across the U.S.  Contributing to the integration of advanced research and quality care at Geisel are D-H's Norris Cotton Cancer Center, Children's Hospital at Dartmouth, The Dartmouth Institute, Synergy Clinical and Translational Science Institute, and multiple clinical group practices around New Hampshire. The Dartmouth Health system is a major contributor to novel medical treatments and health science research, and the site of numerous clinical trials.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
Our Mission: 
-To improve the lives of the communities we serve through inclusive excellence in learning, discovery, and healing.
-To foster an inclusive, diverse community that reflects our world and addresses the most challenging issues in healthcare.
 
At Geisel, our Vision is to be the medical school that sets the standard for educating humanistic physicians, scientists, and educators to be leaders of change and to flourish in their chosen paths . We strive to build a diverse and inclusive community reflective of our world in order to enrich learning, foster innovation, and help tackle the most vexing challenges in health care. We aim to do this by cultivating character, a growth mindset and servant leadership qualities in our students so that they may best serve our communities locally and globally to live healthier and fulfilled lives.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: If your school has a premedical committee, we require a composite recommendation from your school's premedical committee or a packet containing a minimum of three individual letters but not more than five. We encourage you to submit letters from a science faculty member and from someone who can speak to your clinical experience. Other letters may come from supervisors, employers, and other colleagues who know you well.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: We encourage you to submit letters from a science faculty member, clinicians, research mentors or work/volunteer supervisors who know you well. Other letters may come from supervisors, employers, and other colleagues. If you are in graduate school, a letter from your thesis advisor is recommended as one of the 3 required letters. Choose letter writers who have supervised you directly and can highlight your strengths and speak to your abilities. We recommend a minimum of 3 and no more than 5 letters.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: The interview day is designed for us to get to know you, and for you to get to know us at Geisel.  The day begins with a welcome from the Associate Dean of Admissions. This is followed by an information session with the admissions team, a brief welcome from the Office of Diversity, Inclusion, and Community Engagement team, and a 20 minute group exercise. In the afternoon, you will have two thirty-minute one-on-one interviews conducted by members of our admissions committee. The day will end with closing remarks from our Associate Dean. Opportunities to connect with our current students will occur separately from the scheduled interview day.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Our interview season begins in late August and continues through March. Interviews take place on Thursdays by invitation only and will be conducted virtually for the 2026-2027 admissions cycle.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Interviews will be conducted virtually for the 2026-2027 admissions cycle.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Applicants with MCAT scores of 503 and above receive the secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: Tuition is the same for all students, regardless of state residency.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: We accept out-of-state applicants. The review process is the same regardless of state residency.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Canadian students are eligible to apply.  The review process is the same regardless of citizenship.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: International students are eligible to apply. The review process is the same regardless of citizenship.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: DACA students are eligible to apply. The review process is the same regardless of citizenship.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
Online Coursework and Labs - We accept online courses from accredited institutions; however, our committee prefers that the majority of your classes be taken in person. Because many colleges and universities moved to fully online/virtual formats due to the COVID-19 pandemic, we will accept online coursework and labs for the 2020-2021 and 2021-2022 academic years. This includes prerequisite courses.

Pass/Fail Coursework - Prerequisite courses must be taken for a grade.  We do accept pass/fail courses for non-prerequisites if they follow the policies of your institution.  Because many colleges and universities  moved to grading courses on a pass/fail or credit/no credit basis due to the COVID-19 pandemic, we will accept credit as reported from your school for any classes impacted by COVID-related modifications. This includes prerequisite courses.

Please find more information at the Geisel School of Medicine website: 
https://geiselmed.dartmouth.edu/admissions/applying/how-to-apply/
https://geiselmed.dartmouth.edu/admissions/applying/admissions-requirements/ and https://geiselmed.dartmouth.edu/admissions/applying/faq/.

Beyond content, class attendance in medical school facilitates social interaction, networking, and engagement in the curriculum.  At the Geisel School of Medicine, we encourage in-person class attendance to harness these benefits.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Our Admissions Committee employs a holistic review process. MCAT scores are considered in the context of one of several academic metrics to ensure a candidate’s preparedness and ability to engage in our rigorous curriculum. The AAMC’s MCAT data is reviewed carefully by our committee to understand and appreciate the variations in scoring. These known variations are considered as part of the holistic review.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: In order to receive a secondary application,  applicants must present an MCAT score of 503 of above.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: There is no minimum undergraduate GPA requirement.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: There is no minimum undergraduate GPA requirement.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We value educational experiences from all institutions of higher learning. Our Admissions Committee understands that every applicant's path to medicine is different and unique, and that our choices are often determined by circumstance and necessity. Holistic review allows us to learn about your individual experience and takes into account distance-traveled for every applicant.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants are welcome to upload additional documents directly to their application in our applicant portal. Application updates might include, but are not limited to, updated grades, a new experience, a publication, letter of continued interest or intent, etc.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Dartmouth’s Geisel School of Medicine seeks to build a diverse and inclusive community to enrich learning, foster innovation, and tackle the most vexing challenges in health care. This is our commitment to all students, including those with disabilities. Medical education requires that the accumulation of scientific knowledge be accompanied by the simultaneous development of specific skills and other competencies. Our technical standards can be found here: https://geiselmed.dartmouth.edu/goaaa/getting-started/esmpg/

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
The Geisel School of Medicine offers need-blind admissions. Application fee waivers are granted to individuals who have received an AMCAS fee waiver. 

All accepted students with documented financial need are offered financial aid packages. Geisel awards scholarships and loans on the basis of need as indicated by the FAFSA, the CSS Profile form, the Geisel financial aid application, and supporting documentation.  For more information, please go to http://geiselmed.dartmouth.edu/admin/fin_aid/.

medSchoolPrograms.info: Students apply to MD/MPH, MD/MBA, MD/M.Eng (Thayer School of Engineering), MD/MHA (Tuck School of Business) and MD/MS (Quantitative Biomedical Sciences, Health Data Science, Epidemiology and Medical Informatics) programs following matriculation, typically during their second year. The MD/MBA program admits up to 7 students per year. The only combined degree program you must apply for during the AMCAS application cycle is the MD/PhD program.

medSchoolPrograms.cname: Dr. Alex Thorngren, Associate Director MD-PhD and TDI PhD Program

medSchoolPrograms.info:
The Dartmouth MD-PhD Undergraduate Summer (MPUS) Fellowship Program is an educational initiative aimed at exposing undergraduates across the US interested in medical science to the vibrant career pathway of the physician-scientist. To this end, the MPUS Fellowship program highly encourages applications from undergraduate students from all backgrounds who are interested in pursuing a dual MD-PhD degree pathway.

During our 8-week long summer program, our Fellows will have the opportunity to:

Conduct Innovative Research
Weekly Clinical Shadowing
Develop Scientific Communication Skills
Career Planning & Mentorship

More information can be found here: https://geiselmed.dartmouth.edu/mpus/welcome/.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: After Feb 20, accepted students may select the “Plan to Enroll” option in AMCAS. If you are certain you will not attend Geisel or another school where you have been accepted, we encourage you to, in writing, withdraw your application as soon as possible. (This professional courtesy aids in class planning and opens a spot for another applicant to be accepted.)
By April 1st, accepted MD-PhD students are required to select "Plan to Enroll" option in AMCAS. Applicants may remain on waitlists at other schools.
After April 15, accepted students, holding acceptances at multiple schools, should narrow their choices to no more than three medical schools. Applicants may remain on waitlists at other schools.
By May 1st, accepted MD students are required to select "Plan to Enroll" option in AMCAS. Applicants may remain on waitlists at other schools.

On May 1st, accepted MD students may select the “Commit to Enroll” option in AMCAS.  This indicates to Geisel that you are withdrawing all acceptances at other medical schools but you may remain on waitlists. If you receive another acceptance offer, you must notify us via e-mail within 24 hours, indicating the name of the school and the amount of time you have to respond to the school’s offer.

By May 1, accepted MD-PhD students are required to select “Commit to Enroll." If “Commit to Enroll” is not selected by this date, the acceptance offer is automatically rescinded, and the application is withdrawn from consideration. Withdrawal from all other waitlists and from any other acceptances is required at this time. Failure to comply will result in the offer of acceptance being rescinded.

By June 1st, accepted MD students are required to select “Commit to Enroll."
If “Commit to Enroll” is not selected by this date, the acceptance offer is automatically rescinded, and the application is withdrawn from consideration. Withdrawal from all other waitlists and from any other acceptances is required at this time. Failure to comply will result in the offer of acceptance being rescinded.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistInformation: The number of waitlist offers fluctuates each year. Our five year average is 30 waitlist offers.
medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: After May 1, we contact waitlisted applicants regarding their desire to remain on the waitlist and admit candidates from the waitlist via a committee process.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: One year (8 semester hours or equivalent) of biology and physics. Two years (16 semester hours or equivalent) of chemistry, which must include one semester (or equivalent) of organic chemistry and one semester (or equivalent) of biochemistry.  One half-year (3 semester hours or equivalent) of college-level mathematics, including either calculus or statistics. Candidates should have completed a minimum of three years of post-secondary study at a US and/or Canadian college or university, have a bachelor's degree, and have pursued a broad range of study in the sciences and humanities that provides a solid foundation in the scientific basis of medicine and in human behavior and society.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: No cut-off date for prerequisite coursework. We encourage students who have been out of school for more than three years to complete some more recent science coursework prior to matriculation.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The Admissions Committee at Geisel carefully reviews the entire candidate application using a holistic review process. We pay special attention to personal, academic, scientific, and community engagement experiences. Our holistic review process places value on applicants who possess a strong academic foundation, a broad range of life experiences, and traits known to promote success in the field of medicine. We look for integrity, compassion, concern for others, grit, coachability, professionalism, resilience, and kindness. We are very intentional about building a class where students will be supportive of one another and will contribute positively to, and benefit from, our institutional mission. Dartmouth does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability, military or veteran status in access to its programs and activities, and in conditions of admission and employment.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: We recommend that applicants demonstrate a reasonable understanding of the American healthcare system and the commitment and rigor required to succeed in the field of medicine.  Direct patient care is valued.  This may be accomplished in many ways including shadowing physicians, volunteer or paid work as a MA, EMT, scribe, or paraprofessional (CNA, RN, etc.).
